Habits that help you
sleep like a rock
Go to bed at the same time every night. Weekends included. Your body loves rhythm, and a steady bedtime makes falling asleep much easier within a couple of weeks.
Keep your bedroom cool and dark. A slightly cold room and blackout curtains tell your body it's time to rest. A warm, bright room keeps your brain half awake.
Put your phone outside the bedroom. Use a cheap alarm clock instead. No late scrolling, no notifications at 2am, and no checking the news the second you wake up.
Stop caffeine after lunch. Coffee stays in your system for hours. A 4pm espresso can still be keeping your mind busy when you're trying to sleep at midnight.
Before: my head raced every night. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer mind that lets go when the lights go out.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: my head raced every night. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now my mind lets go at night.

slides.texte_overlay: Get daylight in the morning. Ten minutes outside after waking sets your body clock, which makes you naturally sleepy at the right time in the evening.
Write tomorrow's to-do list before bed. Getting tasks out of your head and onto paper stops your mind from running through them while you're trying to rest.
